stories.headline: Dem eyeing Homeland Security committee's oversight subcommittee gavel aims 'to dismantle DHS from the inside'
stories.note: A Democrat openly vowing to gut DHS hands Republicans a ready-made border-security contrast.
body: Rep. Ramirez, a House Democrat who just won re-election in the 2026 midterms, says she is going after the chair of the House Homeland Security Committee's oversight and investigations subcommittee once Democrats take the majority next year.

In an interview with Mother Jones, she made her goal plain. She said she has already filed a bill to dismantle the Department of Homeland Security and intends to "dismantle DHS from the inside" through the subcommittee's investigations.

Ramirez said probes into detention, contractors and the 287(g) programs that let local police work with federal immigration agents would build the case. She described a reimagined setup that keeps cybersecurity, FEMA, TSA and customs, but abolishes ICE and CBP and moves their money to healthcare and community programs.

She also tied the effort to a broader progressive wish list, saying Congress should pass Medicare for All, raise wages, abolish super PACs and tax the rich, while holding officials she called fascists in the administration accountable.
The White House, DHS and Ramirez's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

Why it matters: A Democrat openly campaigning to abolish ICE and CBP from a powerful oversight perch gives Republicans a clear, ready-made border-security contrast as the new Democratic majorities take over.

stories.headline: Democrats plot massive spending spree after midterm rout — and Trump could help them pull it off
stories.note: Dems' big-spending plans give the GOP a clear inflation-and-debt message heading into the new Congress.
body: Fresh off their midterm wins, incoming Democrats are already lining up a major expansion of federal spending: more healthcare money, direct checks to voters, restored housing aid and reversals of cuts to the federal workforce, with tax changes meant to pay for it.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries laid out a first-100-days list in a Nov. 4 manifesto that includes reversing Medicaid cuts, restoring SNAP funding, extending Affordable Care Act tax credits and scrapping Trump's tariffs.

The price tags are steep. The CBO estimates that making the enhanced ACA credits permanent would add about $350 billion to deficits through 2035, and the article notes the annual deficit neared $2 trillion in fiscal 2026, with interest on the debt alone topping $1 trillion.

Democrats still can't override a veto, so they'll need the White House or GOP votes. Spokeswoman Olivia Wales said Trump will work with anyone who wants to lower costs, but warned that if Democrats "choose to pursue radical-left policies," they are working against Americans' interests.
Cato's Michael Cannon argued the GOP didn't lose seats over healthcare and that the expired subsidies helped people earning up to $600,000 a year, urging the president not to cave.
Why it matters: A Democratic spending binge on top of a ballooning deficit hands Republicans a strong inflation-and-debt message, and a chance to draw firm lines in negotiations.

stories.headline: Federal prosecutor warns Sen Warren of 'legal consequences' if records aren't preserved in Trump-linked probes
stories.note: A federal prosecutor is putting Elizabeth Warren on notice, turning the tables on Dem investigators.
body: Aaron Reitz, the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Texas, sent Sen. Elizabeth Warren a letter Sunday demanding she preserve records tied to investigations she may launch once she takes over the Senate Banking Committee in January.

Reitz accused Warren of planning to target private individuals close to President Trump, writing that she appears "eager to wield your future gavel like a tomahawk." The letter and his social media post were peppered with Native American references that poke at her past heritage claims.

The notice warns that failing to keep the documents could bring sanctions or "significant legal consequences," and gives Warren until 6 p.m. ET on Nov. 23 to confirm she has taken steps to preserve them.

Reitz pointed to Warren's Nov. 8 'Face the Nation' appearance, where she talked about investigating Big Tech and Wall Street leaders. Sens. Richard Blumenthal and Elissa Slotkin got similar letters, and Rep. Robert Garcia received one from White House Counsel Will Scharf.

The article notes the letter doesn't establish Warren broke any law, and that legitimate congressional probes generally enjoy Speech or Debate Clause protection. Attorney General Todd Blanche has said there are no criminal investigations into incoming lawmakers' words.
Why it matters: The administration is putting Democrats on notice before they even pick up their gavels, signaling that payback-style investigations of Trump allies will face pushback.

stories.headline: White House calls DC policies 'insanity' after 19-year-old gunman gets probation in shooting
stories.note: A probation-only sentence for a gunman spotlights soft-on-crime policies and backs Trump's DC crackdown case.
body: A 19-year-old prosecutors say fired more than 20 rounds into a Northwest Washington neighborhood, wounding a boy playing basketball, has walked free on probation, and the White House is calling D.C.'s sentencing rules "insanity."

Prosecutors wanted Darius Drew locked up for five years. Instead, Superior Court Judge Jennifer Di Toro suspended a two-year sentence and gave him 18 months of supervised probation under D.C.'s Youth Rehabilitation Act, over the government's objection. Drew had pleaded guilty to aggravated assault and carrying a pistol without a license.

According to prosecutors, surveillance video caught Drew firing at a parked car on May 11 before shooting toward a house; the boy was hit in the leg. Investigators later found two guns, ammunition and suspected narcotics at his home. He was released Friday after nearly six months in custody.

U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro had warned the D.C. Council in August 2025 to overhaul the law, which lets offenders under 25 get below mandatory minimums. Her office says 96% of under-25 felony defendants from 2022 through 2024 were eligible for it.

White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said that even with such policies in place, Trump's Safe and Beautiful Task Force has driven down violent crime in the capital; the White House says the operation has made more than 19,000 arrests.
Why it matters: The case is a vivid example of the soft-on-crime approach Republicans have campaigned against, and it strengthens the argument for Trump's federal crime push in D.C.

stories.headline: NYC DSA urges AOC to run for president while planning to take over City Council
stories.note: Socialists pushing AOC for 2028 deepens the Democrats' left-wing identity problem.
body: New York City's Democratic Socialists of America voted 291 to 123 at their annual convention Saturday to urge Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president in 2028.

Chapter co-chair Gustavo Gordillo said the vote isn't a formal endorsement but a commitment to building the foundation for a presidential run, adding that DSA will "create the conditions for a presidential campaign."
The chapter also mapped out plans to take over the New York City Council, among other resolutions.

There was an awkward twist: Politico reported that several resolutions appeared AI-generated, with the 2029 City Council plan rated 100% AI by the Pangram detector, even though the group has a policy against AI and voted to oppose its expansion. Co-chair Grace Mausser said she was highly skeptical of the results.

Why it matters: Socialists rallying behind AOC for 2028 and plotting to run New York's council deepens the Democrats' left-wing identity problem, a gift for Republicans looking to paint the party as captured by its fringe.
